title: These $32 Running Headphones Light Up at Night to Keep You Safe On Your Evening Walk or Run
summary: The HAKII Light 2 headphones feature a light up headband that emits a bright green glow to keep you visible in dark conditions.
contentText:

Summer is rolling into fall and the sun is setting earlier at night, making it a little more dangerous if you’re used to going on an evening run .

Fortunately, we’ve spotted a new pair of headphones on Amazon that let you take your walk or run into the late nights while making sure you stay visible. These HAKII Light 2 headphones feature a light up headband that emits a bright green glow, making sure you’re well-lit, even in dark neighborhoods.

The wrap around design means the entire back of your head is lit up, lending a halo-style effect to keep you fully in view. It’s more effective than running vests or armbands with reflective patches, which only show up when a light is pointed in their direction. These light-up headphones stay bright the entire time, making sure you’re visible to drivers, cyclists and other pedestrians.

Of course, these are headphones designed for music too , and the HAKII Light 2 features surprisingly powerful sound with big bass, to boost your running playlist. The adjustable headband features a comfortable over-ear design that helps the headphones stay in place even as you’re moving.

The wireless headphones are also rated IPX5 to be sweat and water-resistant — no need to worry if you’re caught in the rain as the music will keep playing. Wipe them down with a towel or cloth to dry.

The HAKII Light 2 portable headphones also use Bluetooth 6.0 technology, one of the latest Bluetooth standards for wireless pairing. What that means: connecting to your phone is super fast and less prone to breaking up.

Of course the light-up headband is why you’ll be buying these headphones, but there’s another safety feature you may not know about: the open-ear design means the earcups rest against your ears rather than covering them up entirely. That allows you to stay aware of your surroundings (say, if a car is approaching or someone is calling out for you) without losing track of your music.
